patch.value: A single transient per-test timeout fails the whole pipeline: 1,942 tests share one uniform 30s budget, no retry is configured, and the only diagnosis path is decoding a blob artifact

A transient test failure is retried a bounded number of times and the retry is recorded, so a single timeout cannot fail the pipeline on its own; Flake occurrences are recorded with test identity, duration and shard so recurrence is a number that can be watched rather than a memory of having seen it before; Per-test timeout budgets are derived from or checked against observed per-test cost, so a test running near its budget is reported as at-risk before it crosses it under load; The failing test name and error appear in the job summary without decoding the coverage blob artifact; A negative control proves a genuinely failing assertion still fails after retries and is never classified as a flake
A transient failure is distinguishable from a real one before it reddens the default branch, and the distinction is recorded rather than re-derived by a human rerun
Every red run that turns out to be transient trains the next reader to rerun first and diagnose second, which is exactly the habit that lets a real regression through.
A tracker-only commit that changes no source file can and did fail CI, so the signal that gates the release path is not currently attributable to the change that triggered it.

Transient timeouts are retried and recorded as flakes with their test identity and duration; a test whose cost approaches its budget is reported before it crosses it; the failing test name is visible without downloading an artifact.
Observed live on commit 1cc62476d, a tracker-and-CHANGELOG-only commit: shard 1 of 4 failed with one timeout out of 1,942 tests while the same file passes locally in 24s for all 30 tests.

message: File the transient-failure policy gap observed on a tracker-only commit

author: harness:claude-code

patch.value:
## The observed failure

Run 31684928972, workflow CI, commit `1cc62476d` on main. That commit changes only `.agents/pm/**` and the generated `CHANGELOG.md`; no file under `src/`, `scripts/`, `docs/` or `.github/` is touched.

```
FAIL tests/unit/commands/test-all-command.spec.ts > runTestAll >
     treats per-test pm_context_mode metadata as part of dedupe identity
Error: Test timed out in 30000ms.
Test Files  1 failed | 122 passed (123)
     Tests  1 failed | 1941 passed (1942)
  Duration  86.90s (transform 16.96s, import 49.51s, tests 166.57s)
```

Every other job on the commit passed: CodeQL, CodSpeed, Docs, Security and Script Quality, OSSF Scorecard, and coverage shards 2, 3 and 4.

## Local reproduction attempt

`node scripts/run-tests.mjs test -- tests/unit/commands/test-all-command.spec.ts` passes all 30 tests in the file in 24.30s, tests 21.19s. The heaviest test in the file takes 4,038ms. The test uses `withTempPmPath`, so it operates on a sandboxed tracker and is structurally independent of the tracker data the commit changed.

So the failure is a timeout under load, not a defect the commit introduced.

## The configuration that turns one timeout into a red branch

`vitest.config.ts` declares `testTimeout: 30_000` and `hookTimeout: 30_000`. There is no `retry` setting, so vitest's default of zero applies. The shard job has `timeout-minutes: 12` and the run itself took 86.9s, so the job was nowhere near its own limit; the per-test budget was the binding constraint.

The budget is uniform across all 1,942 tests. Most complete in hundreds of milliseconds. A handful spawn subprocesses and are an order of magnitude slower. Under CI contention the slowest of those is the one that crosses 30s, and with no retry, crossing it once is sufficient to fail the pipeline.

## Why the diagnosis path makes this worse

The shard's console output ends at "blob report written to .vitest-reports/blob-1.json" and "Process completed with exit code 1". The failing test name is present in the raw log but there is no job summary carrying it, so the practical route to a diagnosis is `gh run view --log-failed` and stripping ANSI escapes, or downloading and decoding the blob artifact. That cost is paid on every red shard regardless of cause, which is precisely the pressure that makes "rerun and see" the rational first move.

## Base rate, stated honestly

Across the last 14 CI runs on main this is the only failure; the two other non-successes were cancellations. So the recurrence rate is not established and this item should not claim the test is chronically flaky. What is established is the policy gap: there is no mechanism that would distinguish a transient timeout from a real failure if it did recur, and no record that would let anyone compute the rate. That is the thing to fix, independently of how often this particular test crosses its budget.

## Boundary

Raising `testTimeout` globally is not the fix. It would hide the at-risk tests rather than report them, and it lengthens the feedback loop for every genuine hang. The fix is bounded retry with the retry recorded, plus a report of tests whose observed cost approaches their budget.
